successors.name: Sarmatians
successors.text: the Pontic steppe: 'By 200 BC, the Sarmatians replaced the Scythians as the dominant people of the steppes'; the Iazyges 'between the Don and Dnieper', the Roxolani 'up to the Dnipro'

successors.name: Scythian Kingdom In Crimea
successors.text: 'the Crimean steppes and foothills, the lower Dnieper, and the lower Southern Bug': Lesser Scythia in Crimea

successors.name: Scythia Minor
successors.text: Lesser Scythia (Scythia Minor) on the lower Danube, in Dobruja

ledger.x: 679 BCE: Bartatua succeeds Išpakaia as king of the Scythians.
679 BCE: the western steppe under Scythian dominion.
672 BCE: the West Asian base at Sakez.
625 BCE: Cyaxares murders the Scythian leaders.

c. 600 BCE: the court leaves the Kuban for the Dnieper. 'The kingdom's centre remained there until c. 600 BC'; Kamianka is the capital 'c. 6th century BC to c. 200 BC', though the text has it become 'the economic, political and commercial capital in the late 5th century BC'. The year is the researcher's…
550 BCE: Ciscaucasia passes to the Sauromatians.
480 BCE: the Istros becomes the border with the Odrysians.
339 BCE: Ateas falls and the Sarmatians cross the Don.
313 BCE: the second defeat; the trans-Don steppe is Sarmatian.
313 BCE: the land east of the Don is lost to the Sarmatians.
313 BCE: the Sarmatian invasion of the Pontic steppe begins.
224 BCE: the Pontic Scythian kingdom ends; the Scythians hold only Crimea and Dobruja.

wars.name: Scythian campaigns in West Asia
wars.outcome: Assyrian vassalage from 672, hegemony over Media 652-625, Urartu conquered c.

wars.name: Scythian campaign of Darius I
wars.outcome: No territorial change: Darius 'crossed the Istros in 513 BC'; he 'claimed to have conquered the Pontic Scythians', Herodotus describes a Scythian victory; 'Some form of Achaemenid authority may have been set up without full annexation'.

wars.name: Ateas' war with Philip II of Macedon
wars.outcome: Macedonian victory: Ateas killed, his army routed, 'The empire of Ateas fell to pieces'; the Scythians 'lost their dominant position in the Pontic steppe for two centuries'.

wars.name: Sarmatian conquest of Scythia
wars.outcome: Sarmatian victory: the Don crossed after 339 and 313 BCE; 'By 200 BC, the Sarmatians replaced the Scythians as the dominant people of the steppes'; the Scythians reduced to Crimea and Dobruja.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the Istros (Danube) is a named border from c.
